NOT SETTLED there: whether an amplitude that has formed no record sources anything; how the field follows a change of its sources (the law is static). (b) FORMATION: an amplitude of energy E spread over a region of radius R forms a record at one site. Compute, for the simplest bond energy, the ledger before (amplitude sourcing, mean field) and after (a point record sourcing): the field's self-energy changes by an amount of order gamma E^2 (G_0(0) - 1/R-type term); give it exactly on the lattice in terms of the potential of the operator (1 - average) (G_0(0) = 1.5164 on Z^3). (c) AMPLITUDE SOURCES: in the mean-field coupling an amplitude in two distant places sources half its energy at each; a test packet passing between them is pulled both ways. State one executed discriminator between (a) and (c) that uses only positions of formed records of the TEST body, and say plainly which assumptions about formation it needs. (d) Say which of the two readings is compatible with each sentence of the Record and Qualification axioms (read the memo in full first). check.py: exact rational evaluation of (b) on a box with walls held at the ambient rate.  DELIVERABLE, in your unit worktree on ai/probes: probes/work/derive/sources-under-the-record-reading/<your worker name>/ATTEMPT.md and check.py. ATTEMPT.md: (1) the exact statement you attempt; (2) numbered steps, each marked PROVED (argument given in full), CHECKED (a finite fact check.py verifies exactly) or ASSUMED; (3) if the route fails, the FIRST step that fails and why: a precise no-go for a route is a result; (4) what would finish it. check.py: exact arithmetic (fractions, integers, sympy) for every finite claim; it prints `SUMMARY: PROVED ...`, `SUMMARY: COUNTEREXAMPLE ...`, `SUMMARY: PARTIAL <what is new and exact>` or `SUMMARY: ROUTE FAILS AT <step>`, and a line `HIT: <the claim>` ONLY when you claim a proof, a counterexample, or a new exact partial result others can build on; a HIT is handed to a worker of another model family to referee line by line, so write for a hostile reader. Rules: definitions come from the notes on the PR branches named above (git fetch origin <branch>; git show origin/<branch>:<note>; find them with gh pr view <n> --json files,headRefName); any outside theorem you use must be re-proved at the scope you use it or listed under ASSUMED; no status words (proved theorems are promoted by the supervisor after the referee). Have your own plan BEFORE reading the prior attempts printed at claim time; then either build on a refereed partial result or take a different route.
